newsitem.title: UK: Britain set to announce health service reforms.
newsitem.headline: Britain set to announce health service reforms.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government said on Thursday it would shortly announce the first in a series of promised reforms to the national health service, including a promise to cut waiting times for some cancer patients.

In the run-up to its crushing May 1 election victory Labour promised to relieve the pressure on the creaking service by cutting some of the bureaucracy which mushroomed after reforms introduced by the outgoing Conservatives.

Health Secretary Frank Dobson said he would be announcing the first changes later on Thursday and added that Labour would stick to its target of reducing waiting times for breast cancer surgery to two weeks.

"I will be able to confirm that there will be savings on management costs this year totalling 100 million pounds ($165 million), some of which we have inherited and new ones which we are pushing through," he told BBC radio.

He deflected questions about possible job losses and concentrated instead on slashing bureaucracy. "I don't know whether anyone will be made redundant but there certainly will be fewer people employed in this grotesque paperchase...and with the money that is saved we can actually do things for patients," he said.
Dobson told the BBC that Labour would gradually make good its pledge to cut breast cancer operation waiting times to a maximum of two weeks but declined to give concrete details.

"About a quarter of the people accepted for cancer treatment have to wait more than a month before they get into hospital for the treatment and we are determined to bring that down...and we're starting with cancer," he said.
